title: Indiquant
summary: Open-source quant research OS for NSE and BSE. The README calls it a Money Radar product by Thugir Group, maintained by Ryan Editraj. Not a trading bot.
body:
Indiquant is a hypothesis-first research loop for Indian markets: propose, backtest, walk-forward, and keep the experiment. The public README names Next.js and FastAPI, with Parquet and DuckDB for the analytics plane, and treats Google Trends as a relative search-demand score rather than absolute volume.

The repository homepage field points at https://moneyradar.in/indiquant. On 23 October 2026 that path returned HTTP 404. The Money Radar root URL returned HTTP 200. His author page on that site calls him founder of MoneyRadar and Thugir Group. The page also says the calculators are not SEBI advice.
homepageNote: README links /indiquant. That path returned 404 on 2026-10-23. Root moneyradar.in returned 200.
role: Maintainer, as stated in the Indiquant README.
verifiedFrom: GitHub repo ryaneditraj/indiquant description and README, fetched 2026-10-23.

title: BTC 1% Radar
summary: A public-data scorecard for BTCUSDT perpetual futures, plus a walk-forward Nifty/NSE research lab. Signal only. No broker keys.
body:
trading-ai scores which side of Bitcoin perpetual futures is likelier to print a ±1% move first, using Binance public futures data: open interest, funding, taker flow, and book depth. The card can print LONG, SHORT, or NO TRADE. A separate lab walk-forward tests Nifty/NSE sleeves.

The README says it is not financial advice and does not route orders. There is no public hosted app. The artifact is the repository.
verifiedFrom: GitHub repo ryaneditraj/trading-ai description and README, fetched 2026-10-23.

title: Trinity One
summary: TuitionOS is the repo. The README names the product Trinity One: the school day on one screen for a tuition centre or school.
body:
Trinity One, in the TuitionOS repository, is described as a mobile-first system for students, faculty, and admins: today’s classes, homework, exams, notes, attendance, and a community board. The README says a session is rejected when the batch, the teacher, or the room is already booked. It names Next.js and TypeScript.

The GitHub homepage field is https://tuition-os-eta.vercel.app. That URL returned HTTP 404 on 23 October 2026, so this site does not call it a live tool. The README names an institution it was built for. That relationship is not independently verified, and the name is not repeated here.
homepageNote: Listed homepage https://tuition-os-eta.vercel.app returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-23.

title: CBSE Physics Predictor
summary: Ranks NCERT Class 12 Physics concepts that repay the next hour of study. Offline. It does not predict a board score.
body:
The README describes tagging question-paper PDFs to NCERT concepts, shrinking noisy year-to-year rates with empirical Bayes, comparing that ranker with gradient boosting in a walk-forward backtest, and turning the winner into an hour-budget plan.

It states it is not affiliated with CBSE or NCERT, and that the bundled fixture is a simulator rather than a set of board papers. There is no hosted product URL.
verifiedFrom: GitHub repo ryaneditraj/cbse-physics-predictor description and README, fetched 2026-10-23.

title: Helmet and triple-riding detection
summary: YOLOv8 for riders without helmets, YOLOv5 for triple riding, and a local Flask dashboard for review.
body:
The repository describes a local computer-vision experiment: a YOLOv8 checkpoint separates riders with and without helmets, and YOLOv5 is used around people and motorcycles for triple riding. Hits are saved as timestamped snapshots and listed on a Flask dashboard.

The README says it is not an official enforcement product and does not read number plates on its own. This page does not describe how to deploy it as surveillance.
verifiedFrom: GitHub repo description and README, fetched 2026-10-23.

title: LayoverBuddy
summary: Ranks layover cities for a route using local JSON. It does not search live fares and it does not book flights.
body:
LayoverBuddy is a Flask app that orders connection cities by a score mixing airport notes, time into town, and how long the stop is. The worked example in the README is Chennai to New York via Singapore, Istanbul, Dubai, or Doha.

Data ships in JSON files. There is no public deployment URL on the repository.

title: KL-ctf
summary: CypherFlag, described in the repo as an autonomous CTF agent harness for a UCSI/Cypherly-style hackathon.
body:
The public repository is an agent harness for authorized capture-the-flag work. This site lists it because it is Ryan’s repo and because cybersecurity shows up as a light thread in the work. It does not reproduce the harness, challenge steps, or any attack procedure.

Read the repository if you are reviewing the project. Do not treat this page as instructions.
verifiedFrom: GitHub repo description, fetched 2026-10-23. Detail beyond that sentence is intentionally omitted.

title: Keeb Keyboard
summary: A 64-key keyboard drawn for Hack Club KEEB: ANSI 60% plus arrows, a Raspberry Pi Pico, KiCad files. The README says it was Ryan’s first PCB.
body:
Keeb Keyboard is hardware: schematic, PCB, Gerbers, and a case. The README says there is no firmware and no app in the repo, and that the pictures were plotted from the design files rather than photographed from a finished board.

The repository description is in the present tense: “I'm Building a keyboard for hackclub KEEB YSWS.”

title: Exam Strategy Studio
summary: A local exam-review log. You record the question, the marks you got, and the marks still on the table. Nothing is uploaded.
body:
The Exam repository’s README names Exam Strategy Studio: a Flask score sheet over a JSON file on your own computer. It is for looking at a class test, a mock, or a past paper after the fact.

No public URL is listed.

title: Travel Personality Analyzer
summary: A 15-question Flask quiz that maps answers to travel styles, then shows destinations, a budget sketch, and a simple itinerary. Answers are not stored.
body:
Personality-Analyzer is a local Flask quiz. The README names four styles: Urban Explorer, Adventure Seeker, Nature Lover, and Cultural Explorer. It does not require an account or an API key.

There is no public deployment URL on the repository.

title: Space 3D site
summary: A Three.js scene made with Hack Club. The repo description says Hack Club is what got Ryan programming again.
body:
Space-3d-site is a browser scene: a textured sphere, a wireframe torus, and simple meshes. It is a Hack Club project, not a product.

Created 3 June 2026.
verifiedFrom: GitHub repo description and profile README, fetched 2026-10-23.

title: Waffles site
summary: A potato-themed page for the Hack Club Waffles program, described in the profile README as a static page with a click counter.
body:
The repository description is Ryan’s: “I made a potato themed site for the hackclub waffles program.” The profile README adds that it is a static page with a click counter, short facts, and a stats page.

It is filed as a finished Hack Club exercise.
verifiedFrom: GitHub description and profile README, fetched 2026-10-23.

title: The CLI Restaurant
summary: A 2022 terminal menu for dine-in orders, later given a Flask page for table requests. No database and no payments.
body:
The README says staff take orders from a command-line menu and guests request a table in the browser. Email is optional. It is MIT licensed and attributed to Ryan Editraj.

The repository was created on 5 April 2022, the same day as the GitHub account.

title: Word Counter
summary: A small Flask word counter. The README says it was made in three hours.
body: Word-Counter is an early Flask exercise from September 2022. The README is one line: a very simple word counter, made in three hours.

title: Restaurant Flask
summary: A restaurant food-ordering system in Flask, from the repository description. The README request returned 404.
body: Restaurant-Flask was created on 8 June 2022. The only description on the repository is “A restaurant food ordering system with flask.” No README was available when this page was written, so nothing further is claimed.

title: Stock Profit Calculator
summary: A simple stock-market profit calculator in Python, from April 2023.
body: The repository description is the whole public claim: a simple stock market profit calculator in Python. It is an early exercise, not the later markets research.

title: Letter Game
summary: A command-line clone of a word game, created the day the GitHub account opened.
body: Letter-Game is described as “A CLI clone of Wordly.” Created 5 April 2022. It sits with the other first-day exercises.

title: Number Guessing Game
summary: A small Python game. The description says it is an app to prevent boredom.
body: Number-Guessing-Game was created on 5 April 2022, minutes after the GitHub account. The description is “A simple app to prevent you against boredom.”

title: Old Portfolio
summary: The repository that held an earlier ryaneditraj.github.io after a newer site replaced it.
body: Old-Portfolio’s description says it was formerly ryaneditraj.github.io, moved aside when a newer version of that site was published. The checked-in page called Ryan a self-taught web and app developer, intermediate in Python, HTML, and CSS. That wording is from March 2023 and is not the current profile README.
